The Hermes Agent desktop app gives you everything the CLI does without touching a terminal — and can even drive an agent running on another machine. Here's the complete guide.

Sign up for my FREE weekly newsletter, where I spill my unfiltered thoughts on the latest AI news, cool research, and projects I'm building: https://www.onchainaigarage.com/

🐦 Follow Tonbi on X for real-time AI x blockchain updates! https://x.com/tonbistudio

A full walkthrough of the new Hermes Agent desktop app (still in beta). The key mental model: it's a front-end, not a separate agent — it drives the exact same Hermes runtime as the CLI and TUI, so the same sessions, memory, skills, and config are all there, and the GUI is decoupled from where the agent actually runs. I install it from scratch, cover the CLI flags worth knowing, and tour the whole UI panel by panel: sessions (and how isolating them per workspace is actually a cost-control feature, not just organization), messaging setup, skills/tools, Cron jobs, the Review Rail preview pane, profiles vs sub-agents (with a live sub-agent run), the per-session file explorer and built-in terminal, and the full settings tour — models, auxiliary slots, safety, voice, and providers. The standout section is remote control: I demo driving one machine's agent from another over the same Wi-Fi, then securely from a VPS over Tailscale so it's never exposed to the open internet — your laptop becomes a window into an agent whose sessions, keys, and memory all stay on the back end. I close with the troubleshooting and clean-reinstall commands that save you when something breaks. It's still early and updated constantly, so I'll keep this guide current — but this is everything the app can do right now.

In this video we break down the best Hermes use cases we have found while running the agent every day, from the new desktop app to cost-aware automations. If you have been on OpenClaw, the hermes agent vs openclaw comparison is simple: the Hermes agent has extra features built in that OpenClaw never had, and that is what makes these use cases hermes can handle so much more powerful.

We start with the new desktop app. It is basically a wrapper around the agent setup, and after testing it we found it is a more interactive way to work than the terminal interface from our previous video. It makes monitoring agents and managing configs easier, and the biggest win for us was running multiple profiles in parallel, where each profile is its own Hermes agent with separate memory and skills. To install Hermes agent, you just download the installer for your operating system and run it, and it carries over the configs you already set up. These hermes desktop use cases alone make the app worth trying, though you can still do everything from the TUI.

Then we get into the use cases hermes agent is actually built for. The first is the Wake Agent feature, a flag in the cron task that decides at runtime whether the Hermes agent should call the LLM at all. If it is set to false, the LLM never fires, so you only pay for tokens when there is a real change worth acting on. This was not possible on OpenClaw, where the agent ran on every cron job. We show how to use it to watch AWS and Gemini API costs and report spikes to a channel, wire up the Stripe MCP to take action, and manage Google Play Store reviews and surface them in Slack.

Next is the no_agent flag, which runs a job without invoking the LLM at all. It still runs inside the Hermes ecosystem, so it has all your context, and we use it to monitor things like TLS and Stripe app health and post the results to Slack. These jobs are practically free, and you can tag Hermes any time you want it to actually act on an alert.

We also cover using the Hermes AI agent as the second brain of your organization by connecting it to Slack, where its evolving memory and skills turn your day to day work into reusable workflows and a company skill the whole team can query. This is one area where the hermes agent vs openclaw gap is clear, since OpenClaw's soul file bloats over time and has to be reset.
After that we get into responding to leads through Gmail using the built-in Google Workspace skills and a webhook, watching competitors by keeping a PRD as a skill and updating it on a weekly cron, and handing off social media with the xurl skill that turns our YouTube scripts into X and LinkedIn posts for review before anything goes live.

These are some of the best Hermes agent use cases for anyone who wants real AI automation instead of another chatbot. If you want the full install Hermes agent walkthrough and config steps, check out our previous video, and grab the longer setup guides from our community in AI Labs Pro. We cover AI, Claude Code, ChatGPT, and tools like this every week, and a lot of our SEO and AI automation workflows run on exactly this setup, so subscribe and hit the bell if these hermes use cases were useful.

Verás cómo usar habilidades preinstaladas, crear tus propias habilidades personalizadas desde cero, configurar la memoria para que tu agente recuerde cómo trabajas, programar trabajos automatizados usando lenguaje natural y gestionar los costos de tu modelo de IA para que nada se acumule sin que lo sepas. También cubro cómo mantener tu agente seguro, cambiar modelos para diferentes trabajos y cuatro funciones extra que puedes explorar por tu cuenta. Ya sea que sea tu primera vez usando un agente de IA o simplemente quieras una guía clara de configuración de Hermes Agent, este recorrido paso a paso tiene todo lo que necesitas.

✔️ Asignar diferentes modelos de IA a diferentes trabajos
✔️ Mantener tu agente seguro desde el primer día
✔️ Mensajes de voz, plataformas adicionales, Skills Hub y soporte MCP
